sanskrit: tena tvam āsāṃ māhātmyaṃ na vettha śṛṇu tat prabho gavāṃ prabhāvaṃ paramaṃ māhātmyaṃ ca surarṣabha
english: Because of this you do not know the greatness of these cows; hear it, O lord. Learn the supreme power and majesty of cattle, O bull among the gods.

sanskrit: yajñāṅgaṃ kathitā gāvo yajña eva ca vāsava etābhiś cāpy ṛte yajño na pravartet kathaṃ cana
english: Cows are declared to be a limb of sacrifice, indeed the very sacrifice itself, O Vāsava; and without them no sacrifice could ever proceed at all.

sanskrit: dhārayanti prajāś caiva payasā haviṣā tathā etāsāṃ tanayāś cāpi kṛṣiyogam upāsate
english: They sustain living beings with their milk and with the oblation; and their offspring too apply themselves to the labor of the plow.

sanskrit: janayanti ca dhānyāni bījāni vividhāni ca tato yajñāḥ pravartante havyaṃ kavyaṃ ca sarvaśaḥ
english: They bring forth grains and seeds of many kinds; from these the sacrifices proceed, and the offerings to the gods and to the ancestors in every form.

sanskrit: payo dadhi ghṛtaṃ caiva puṇyāś caitāḥ surādhipa vahanti vividhān bhārān kṣuttṛṣṇāparipīḍitāḥ
english: Milk, curds, and clarified butter—holy are these cows, O lord of the gods; and tormented by hunger and thirst they bear burdens of every kind.

sanskrit: munīṃś ca dhārayantīha prajāś caivāpi karmaṇā vāsavākūṭavāhinyaḥ karmaṇā sukṛtena ca upariṣṭāt tato 'smākaṃ vasanty etāḥ sadaiva hi
english: By their toil they sustain the sages here and all living beings as well, O Vāsava; drawing their loads with guileless hearts, and by their meritorious deeds, they dwell forever above even us.

sanskrit: etat te kāraṇaṃ śakra nivāsakṛtam adya vai gavāṃ devopariṣṭād dhi samākhyātaṃ śatakrato
english: This, O Śakra, is the reason I have now told you why the abode of cattle lies above even the gods, O lord of a hundred sacrifices.

sanskrit: etā hi varadattāś ca varadāś caiva vāsava saurabhyaḥ puṇyakarmiṇyaḥ pāvanāḥ śubhalakṣaṇāḥ
english: For these cows are both granted by boon and themselves bestowers of boons, O Vāsava—daughters of Surabhī, doers of holy deeds, purifying, and marked with auspicious signs.

sanskrit: yadarthaṃ gā gatāś caiva saurabhyaḥ surasattama tac ca me śṛṇu kārtsnyena vadato balasūdana
english: And for what reason the daughters of Surabhī attained the rank of cattle, O best of the gods—hear that too in full as I tell it, O slayer of Bala.

sanskrit: purā devayuge tāta daityendreṣu mahātmasu trīṃl lokān anuśāsatsu viṣṇau garbhatvam āgate
english: Of old, in the age of the gods, dear one, when the great-souled lords of the Daityas were ruling the three worlds, Viṣṇu entered the womb.

sanskrit: adityās tapyamānāyās tapo ghoraṃ suduścaram putrārtham amaraśreṣṭha pādenaikena nityadā
english: While Aditi was practicing fearsome and most difficult austerity, standing ever upon a single foot for the sake of a son, O best of the immortals—

sanskrit: tāṃ tu dṛṣṭvā mahādevīṃ tapyamānāṃ mahat tapaḥ dakṣasya duhitā devī surabhir nāma nāmataḥ
english: and seeing that great goddess engaged in mighty austerity, the goddess who was Dakṣa's daughter, Surabhī by name,

sanskrit: atapyata tapo ghoraṃ hṛṣṭā dharmaparāyaṇā kailāsaśikhare ramye devagandharvasevite
english: in gladness, devoted to dharma, performed a fearsome austerity upon the lovely peak of Kailāsa, frequented by gods and Gandharvas.

sanskrit: vyatiṣṭhad ekapādena paramaṃ yogam āsthitā daśa varṣasahasrāṇi daśa varṣaśatāni ca
english: Established in supreme yoga, she stood upon a single foot for ten thousand years and ten hundred years besides.

sanskrit: saṃtaptās tapasā tasyā devāḥ sarṣimahoragāḥ tatra gatvā mayā sārdhaṃ paryupāsanta tāṃ śubhām
english: Scorched by the heat of her austerity, the gods together with the sages and the great serpents went there with me and waited upon that auspicious one.

sanskrit: athāham abruvaṃ tatra devīṃ tāṃ tapasānvitām kimarthaṃ tapyate devi tapo ghoram anindite
english: Then I spoke there to that goddess girt with austerity: 'For what purpose, O goddess, do you practice this fearsome austerity, O blameless one?'

sanskrit: prītas te 'haṃ mahābhāge tapasānena śobhane varayasva varaṃ devi dātāsmīti puraṃdara
english: 'I am pleased with you, O fortunate one, by this austerity, O lovely one; choose a boon, O goddess, for I am ready to grant it'—so said Brahmā, O Purandara.

sanskrit: surabhy uvāca vareṇa bhagavan mahyaṃ kṛtaṃ lokapitāmaha eṣa eva varo me 'dya yat prīto 'si mamānagha
english: Surabhī said: By a boon, O blessed one, my purpose is fulfilled, O grandsire of the worlds; this very thing is my boon today—that you are pleased with me, O sinless one.

sanskrit: brahmovāca tām evaṃ bruvatīṃ devīṃ surabhīṃ tridaśeśvara pratyabruvaṃ yad devendra tan nibodha śacīpate
english: Brahmā said: To the goddess Surabhī, who spoke thus, O lord of the thirty gods, I made reply—learn now what I said, O king of the gods, O consort of Śacī.

sanskrit: alobhakāmyayā devi tapasā ca śubhena te prasanno 'haṃ varaṃ tasmād amaratvaṃ dadāni te
english: 'By your freedom from greed and desire, O goddess, and by your holy austerity, I am well pleased; therefore I grant you the boon of immortality.'

sanskrit: trayāṇām api lokānām upariṣṭān nivatsyasi matprasādāc ca vikhyāto golokaḥ sa bhaviṣyati
english: 'Above even the three worlds shall you dwell, and by my favor that place shall become renowned as the World of Cattle, Goloka.'

sanskrit: mānuṣeṣu ca kurvāṇāḥ prajāḥ karma sutās tava nivatsyanti mahābhāge sarvā duhitaraś ca te
english: 'And your sons, doing their work among men, and all your daughters too shall dwell there, O fortunate one.'

sanskrit: manasā cintitā bhogās tvayā vai divyamānuṣāḥ yac ca svargasukhaṃ devi tat te saṃpatsyate śubhe
english: 'Whatever enjoyments, divine and human, you conceive in your mind, and whatever happiness of heaven there is, O goddess—all that shall be yours, O auspicious one.'

sanskrit: tasyā lokāḥ sahasrākṣa sarvakāmasamanvitāḥ na tatra kramate mṛtyur na jarā na ca pāvakaḥ na dainyaṃ nāśubhaṃ kiṃ cid vidyate tatra vāsava
english: Her worlds, O thousand-eyed one, are furnished with every desire; there death does not advance, nor old age, nor fire; no misery and nothing inauspicious is found there, O Vāsava.

sanskrit: tatra divyāny araṇyāni divyāni bhavanāni ca vimānāni ca yuktāni kāmagāni ca vāsava
english: There are divine forests there, and divine dwellings, and well-appointed celestial chariots that go where one wishes, O Vāsava.

sanskrit: vrataiś ca vividhaiḥ puṇyais tathā tīrthānusevanāt tapasā mahatā caiva sukṛtena ca karmaṇā śakyaḥ samāsādayituṃ golokaḥ puṣkarekṣaṇa
english: By holy vows of many kinds, by frequenting sacred fords, by great austerity, and by good works, Goloka can be attained, O lotus-eyed one.

sanskrit: etat te sarvam ākhyātaṃ mayā śakrānupṛcchate na te paribhavaḥ kāryo gavām arinisūdana
english: All this I have declared to you, O Śakra, who asked of it; you must show no contempt for cattle, O slayer of foes.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca etac chrutvā sahasrākṣaḥ pūjayām āsa nityadā gāś cakre bahumānaṃ ca tāsu nityaṃ yudhiṣṭhira
english: Bhīṣma said: Having heard this, the thousand-eyed one ever honored cattle and always held them in high esteem, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: etat te sarvam ākhyātaṃ pāvanaṃ ca mahādyute pavitraṃ paramaṃ cāpi gavāṃ māhātmyam uttamam kīrtitaṃ puruṣavyāghra sarvapāpavināśanam
english: All this I have told you, purifying and of great splendor; the supremely holy and highest greatness of cattle has been proclaimed, O tiger among men—a thing that destroys all sins.

sanskrit: ya idaṃ kathayen nityaṃ brāhmaṇebhyaḥ samāhitaḥ havyakavyeṣu yajñeṣu pitṛkāryeṣu caiva ha sārvakāmikam akṣayyaṃ pitṝṃs tasyopatiṣṭhati
english: Whoever, with collected mind, recounts this always to the brāhmaṇas—at the offerings to gods and ancestors, at sacrifices, and at the rites for the fathers—an imperishable reward fulfilling every desire awaits his ancestors.

sanskrit: goṣu bhaktaś ca labhate yad yad icchati mānavaḥ striyo 'pi bhaktā yā goṣu tāś ca kāmān avāpnuyuḥ
english: The man devoted to cattle obtains whatever he desires; and women too who are devoted to cattle attain their wishes.

sanskrit: putrārthī labhate putraṃ kanyā patim avāpnuyāt dhanārthī labhate vittaṃ dharmārthī dharmam āpnuyāt
english: He who longs for a son obtains a son; the maiden gains a husband; he who seeks wealth gains riches; he who seeks dharma attains dharma.

sanskrit: vidyārthī prāpnuyād vidyāṃ sukhārthī prāpnuyāt sukham na kiṃ cid durlabhaṃ caiva gavāṃ bhaktasya bhārata
english: He who seeks knowledge attains knowledge; he who seeks happiness attains happiness; for him who is devoted to cattle nothing is hard to win, O descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca uktaṃ pitāmahenedaṃ gavāṃ dānam anuttamam viśeṣeṇa narendrāṇām iti dharmam avekṣatām
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: The grandsire has declared this—that the gift of cattle is unsurpassed, and especially so for kings who keep their gaze upon dharma.

sanskrit: rājyaṃ hi satataṃ duḥkham āśramāś ca sudurvidāḥ parivāreṇa vai duḥkhaṃ durdharaṃ cākṛtātmabhiḥ bhūyiṣṭhaṃ ca narendrāṇāṃ vidyate na śubhā gatiḥ
english: For kingship is unceasing sorrow, and the orders of life are very hard to know; with a great retinue comes grief, hard to bear for those whose souls are unperfected; and most often no auspicious destiny is found for kings.

sanskrit: pūyante te 'tra niyataṃ prayacchanto vasuṃdharām pūrvaṃ ca kathitā dharmās tvayā me kurunandana
english: They are surely purified herein who bestow the gift of land; and the duties you have already related to me before, O joy of the Kurus.

sanskrit: evam eva gavām uktaṃ pradānaṃ te nṛgeṇa ha ṛṣiṇā nāciketena pūrvam eva nidarśitam
english: Just so the gift of cattle was extolled by you, as it was shown of old by King Nṛga and by the sage Nāciketa.

sanskrit: vedopaniṣade caiva sarvakarmasu dakṣiṇā sarvakratuṣu coddiṣṭaṃ bhūmir gāvo 'tha kāñcanam
english: And in the Vedas and the Upaniṣads, in all rites the sacrificial fee is enjoined, and in all sacrifices: land, cattle, and gold.

sanskrit: tatra śrutis tu paramā suvarṇaṃ dakṣiṇeti vai etad icchāmy ahaṃ śrotuṃ pitāmaha yathātatham
english: Therein the supreme scriptural teaching is that gold is the fitting fee; this I wish to hear, O grandsire, exactly as it is.

sanskrit: kiṃ suvarṇaṃ kathaṃ jātaṃ kasmin kāle kim ātmakam kiṃ dānaṃ kiṃ phalaṃ caiva kasmāc ca param ucyate
english: What is gold, how did it come to be, in what age, and of what nature? What is its gift, what is its fruit, and why is it called the highest?

sanskrit: kasmād dānaṃ suvarṇasya pūjayanti manīṣiṇaḥ kasmāc ca dakṣiṇārthaṃ tad yajñakarmasu śasyate
english: Why do the wise honor the gift of gold, and why is it commended as the fee in the rites of sacrifice?

sanskrit: kasmāc ca pāvanaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ bhūmer gobhyaś ca kāñcanam paramaṃ dakṣiṇārthe ca tad bravīhi pitāmaha
english: And why is gold the most purifying—above land and above cattle—and supreme as a sacrificial fee? Tell me this, O grandsire.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca śṛṇu rājann avahito bahukāraṇavistaram jātarūpasamutpattim anubhūtaṃ ca yan mayā
english: Bhīṣma said: Listen attentively, O king, to the full account of its many causes—the origin of gold and what I myself have experienced.

sanskrit: pitā mama mahātejāḥ śaṃtanur nidhanaṃ gataḥ tasya ditsur ahaṃ śrāddhaṃ gaṅgādvāram upāgamam
english: My father, the greatly resplendent Śaṃtanu, had passed away; wishing to perform his śrāddha rite, I came to the Gate of Gaṅgā.

sanskrit: tatrāgamya pituḥ putra śrāddhakarma samārabham mātā me jāhnavī caiva sāhāyyam akarot tadā
english: Having arrived there, my son, I began the śrāddha rite for my father, and my mother Jāhnavī then lent me her aid.

sanskrit: tato 'gratas tapaḥsiddhān upaveśya bahūn ṛṣīn toyapradānāt prabhṛti kāryāṇy aham athārabham
english: Then, having seated before me many sages perfected in austerity, I began the rites, beginning with the offering of water.

sanskrit: tat samāpya yathoddiṣṭaṃ pūrvakarma samāhitaḥ dātuṃ nirvapaṇaṃ samyag yathāvad aham ārabham
english: Having completed that preliminary rite as prescribed, with collected mind I set about offering the funeral oblation rightly, in due order.

sanskrit: tatas taṃ darbhavinyāsaṃ bhittvā surucirāṅgadaḥ pralambābharaṇo bāhur udatiṣṭhad viśāṃ pate
english: Then, breaking through that arrangement of darbha grass, an arm rose up, adorned with a lovely armlet and with pendent ornaments, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: tam utthitam ahaṃ dṛṣṭvā paraṃ vismayam āgamam pratigrahītā sākṣān me piteti bharatarṣabha
english: Seeing it risen up, I fell into utter astonishment, thinking, 'It is my father in person, come to receive the offering,' O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: tato me punar evāsīt saṃjñā saṃcintya śāstrataḥ nāyaṃ vedeṣu vihito vidhir hasta iti prabho piṇḍo deyo nareṇeha tato matir abhūn mama
english: Then my reason returned to me, and reflecting upon the scriptures I thought: 'This rule is not enjoined in the Vedas—that the offering be placed into a hand'; and this conviction arose in me, O lord.

sanskrit: sākṣān neha manuṣyasya pitaro 'ntarhitāḥ kva cit gṛhṇanti vihitaṃ tv evaṃ piṇḍo deyaḥ kuśeṣv iti
english: 'A man's fathers, being hidden from sight, do not anywhere receive it directly; it is thus enjoined that the rice-ball be offered upon the kuśa grass.'

sanskrit: tato 'haṃ tad anādṛtya pitur hastanidarśanam śāstrapramāṇāt sūkṣmaṃ tu vidhiṃ pārthiva saṃsmaran
english: Then, disregarding the appearance of my father's hand, mindful of the subtle rule on the authority of scripture, O king—

sanskrit: tato darbheṣu tat sarvam adadaṃ bharatarṣabha śāstramārgānusāreṇa tad viddhi manujarṣabha
english: I offered all of it upon the darbha grass, O bull of the Bhāratas, following the path of scripture; know this, O bull among men.

sanskrit: tataḥ so 'ntarhito bāhuḥ pitur mama narādhipa tato māṃ darśayām āsuḥ svapnānte pitaras tadā
english: Thereupon that arm of my father vanished, O ruler of men; and then the fathers showed themselves to me at the close of a dream.

sanskrit: prīyamāṇās tu mām ūcuḥ prītāḥ sma bharatarṣabha vijñānena tavānena yan na muhyasi dharmataḥ
english: And being well pleased they said to me: 'We are pleased, O bull of the Bhāratas, by this discernment of yours, in that you are not led astray from dharma.'

sanskrit: tvayā hi kurvatā śāstraṃ pramāṇam iha pārthiva ātmā dharmaḥ śrutaṃ vedāḥ pitaraś ca maharṣibhiḥ
english: 'For by making scripture your authority herein, O king, you have honored—as the great sages do—the self, dharma, sacred learning, the Vedas, and the fathers.'

sanskrit: sākṣāt pitāmaho brahmā guravo 'tha prajāpatiḥ pramāṇam upanītā vai sthitiś ca na vicālitā
english: 'The grandsire Brahmā himself, the teachers, and Prajāpati have been upheld as authority, and the established order has not been shaken.'

sanskrit: tad idaṃ samyag ārabdhaṃ tvayādya bharatarṣabha kiṃ tu bhūmer gavāṃ cārthe suvarṇaṃ dīyatām iti
english: 'This rite has been rightly begun by you today, O bull of the Bhāratas; but for the sake of land and cattle, let gold be given.'

sanskrit: evaṃ vayaṃ ca dharmaś ca sarve cāsmatpitāmahāḥ pāvitā vai bhaviṣyanti pāvanaṃ paramaṃ hi tat
english: 'Thus shall we, and dharma, and all our forefathers be purified; for that is the highest purification.'

sanskrit: daśa pūrvān daśa parāṃs tathā saṃtārayanti te suvarṇaṃ ye prayacchanti evaṃ me pitaro 'bruvan
english: 'Those who bestow gold carry across ten ancestors before them and ten descendants after'—thus did my fathers speak to me.

sanskrit: tato 'haṃ vismito rājan pratibuddho viśāṃ pate suvarṇadāne 'karavaṃ matiṃ bharatasattama
english: Then, awakened in astonishment, O king, O lord of peoples, I set my mind upon the gift of gold, O best of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: itihāsam imaṃ cāpi śṛṇu rājan purātanam jāmadagnyaṃ prati vibho dhanyam āyuṣyam eva ca
english: Hear too this ancient tale, O king, concerning the son of Jamadagni, O mighty one—a tale that bestows fortune and long life.

sanskrit: jāmadagnyena rāmeṇa tīvraroṣānvitena vai triḥsaptakṛtvaḥ pṛthivī kṛtā niḥkṣatriyā purā
english: By Rāma, the son of Jamadagni, filled with fierce wrath, the earth was made bereft of warriors thrice seven times of old.

sanskrit: tato jitvā mahīṃ kṛtsnāṃ rāmo rājīvalocanaḥ ājahāra kratuṃ vīro brahmakṣatreṇa pūjitam
english: Then, having conquered the whole earth, the lotus-eyed hero Rāma performed a sacrifice honored by brāhmaṇas and kṣatriyas alike.

sanskrit: vājimedhaṃ mahārāja sarvakāmasamanvitam pāvanaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ tejodyutivivardhanam
english: A horse-sacrifice, O great king, furnished with every desired thing, purifying to all beings and enhancing splendor and luster.

sanskrit: vipāpmāpi sa tejasvī tena kratuphalena vai naivātmano 'tha laghutāṃ jāmadagnyo 'bhyagacchata
english: Though already free of sin, that resplendent son of Jamadagni did not, even by the fruit of that sacrifice, reach lightness in his own esteem.

sanskrit: sa tu kratuvareṇeṣṭvā mahātmā dakṣiṇāvatā papracchāgamasaṃpannān ṛṣīn devāṃś ca bhārgavaḥ
english: Having worshipped with that most excellent, fee-laden sacrifice, the great-souled scion of Bhṛgu questioned the sages and the gods, who were learned in scripture.

sanskrit: pāvanaṃ yat paraṃ nṝṇām ugre karmaṇi vartatām tad ucyatāṃ mahābhāgā iti jātaghṛṇo 'bravīt
english: 'Let it be told, O greatly fortunate ones, what is the supreme purification for men engaged in dread and violent deeds'—so spoke he in whom compassion had arisen.

sanskrit: vasiṣṭha uvāca devatās te prayacchanti suvarṇaṃ ye dadaty uta agnir hi devatāḥ sarvāḥ suvarṇaṃ ca tad ātmakam
english: Vasiṣṭha said: They who give gold bestow the very gods; for Agni is all the gods, and gold is of that same essence.

sanskrit: tasmāt suvarṇaṃ dadatā dattāḥ sarvāś ca devatāḥ bhavanti puruṣavyāghra na hy ataḥ paramaṃ viduḥ
english: Therefore by him who gives gold all the gods are given, O tiger among men; for they know of nothing higher than this.

sanskrit: bhūya eva ca māhātmyaṃ suvarṇasya nibodha me gadato mama viprarṣe sarvaśastrabhṛtāṃ vara
english: And learn yet further the greatness of gold as I tell it, O sage among brāhmaṇas, O best of all who bear weapons.

sanskrit: mayā śrutam idaṃ pūrvaṃ purāṇe bhṛgunandana prajāpateḥ kathayato manoḥ svāyaṃbhuvasya vai
english: This I heard of old in the ancient lore, O joy of the Bhṛgus, as the Prajāpati Manu, the self-existent, related it.

sanskrit: śūlapāṇer bhagavato rudrasya ca mahātmanaḥ girau himavati śreṣṭhe tadā bhṛgukulodvaha
english: It concerns the trident-bearing lord, the great-souled Rudra, upon the most excellent mountain Himavat, O upholder of the Bhṛgu line.

sanskrit: devyā vivāhe nirvṛtte rudrāṇyā bhṛgunandana samāgame bhagavato devyā saha mahātmanaḥ tataḥ sarve samudvignā bhagavantam upāgaman
english: When the wedding of the goddess Rudrāṇī had been accomplished, O joy of the Bhṛgus, and the great-souled lord came together with the goddess, then all the gods, deeply agitated, approached the lord.

sanskrit: te mahādevam āsīnaṃ devīṃ ca varadām umām prasādya śirasā sarve rudram ūcur bhṛgūdvaha
english: Having propitiated with bowed heads the seated Mahādeva and the boon-granting goddess Umā, they all spoke to Rudra, O upholder of the Bhṛgus.

sanskrit: ayaṃ samāgamo deva devyā saha tavānagha tapasvinas tapasvinyā tejasvinyātitejasaḥ amoghatejās tvaṃ deva devī ceyam umā tathā
english: 'This union of yours with the goddess, O sinless god—of you, an ascetic, with her, an ascetic; of you, supremely fiery, with her, the fiery one—O god, your fire is unfailing, and so too is this goddess Umā.'

sanskrit: apatyaṃ yuvayor deva balavad bhavitā prabho tan nūnaṃ triṣu lokeṣu na kiṃ cic cheṣayiṣyati
english: 'The offspring of you two, O god, will be mighty, O lord; surely it will leave nothing remaining in the three worlds.'

sanskrit: tad ebhyaḥ praṇatebhyas tvaṃ devebhyaḥ pṛthulocana varaṃ prayaccha lokeśa trailokyahitakāmyayā apatyārthaṃ nigṛhṇīṣva tejo jvalitam uttamam
english: 'Therefore to these gods who bow before you, O broad-eyed one, grant a boon, O lord of the worlds, out of desire for the welfare of the three worlds: for the sake of progeny, restrain your blazing, supreme seed.'

sanskrit: iti teṣāṃ kathayatāṃ bhagavān govṛṣadhvajaḥ evam astv iti devāṃs tān viprarṣe pratyabhāṣata
english: As they spoke thus, the blessed lord whose banner bears the bull replied to those gods, O sage among brāhmaṇas: 'So be it.'

sanskrit: ity uktvā cordhvam anayat tad reto vṛṣavāhanaḥ ūrdhvaretāḥ samabhavat tataḥprabhṛti cāpi saḥ
english: Having said this, the bull-borne lord drew his seed upward; and from that time forth he became one whose seed flows upward.
